topics.title: Fashion Portfolio Development Co
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify the components of a fashion portfolio.
The students should be able to differentiate between digital and physical portfolios.
The students should be able to create a simple physical portfolio layout.
The students should be able to explain the importance of a portfolio in fashion design.
Introduction:
Today we will learn about fashion portfolios, which are important for showcasing your design work. We have already learned about different types of garments and design techniques, and now we need to know how to present our work professionally.
Content:
A fashion portfolio is a collection of your best design work that demonstrates your skills, creativity, and style as a designer. It is like a resume for fashion designers, showing potential clients or employers what you can do.
Components of a fashion portfolio include:
1. Title page with your name and contact information
2. Personal statement about your design philosophy
3. Mood boards that show your inspiration
4. Design sketches with fabric samples
5. Photographs of finished garments
6. Details of any sewing techniques used
Digital portfolios are electronic collections that can be shared online through websites, social media, or email. They are convenient for reaching a wider audience and can include videos of garments in motion. For example, a Nigerian designer might use Instagram to showcase their Ankara designs to potential customers abroad.
Physical portfolios are printed or bound collections that you can carry to meetings or interviews. They allow people to touch fabric samples and see details up close. In Nigeria, physical portfolios are often presented to boutique owners at markets like Balogun Market in Lagos.
Creating a portfolio involves selecting your best work, arranging it in a logical order, and ensuring consistent presentation. Remember to keep your portfolio updated as you create new designs.
Class activity:
Students will create a simple physical portfolio by selecting their best design sketches from the term. They will arrange these sketches in a logical order, add fabric samples where possible, and create a title page with their name and a brief personal statement about their design interests.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is a fashion portfolio?
2. List three components that should be included in a fashion portfolio.
3. How is a digital portfolio different from a physical portfolio?
4. Why is it important for a fashion designer to have a portfolio?
5. Name one Nigerian market where a physical portfolio might be presented to potential clients.
Summary:
A fashion portfolio is essential for showcasing your design skills to potential clients and employers, and can be either digital or physical depending on your needs and audience.

topics.title: Presentation Skills
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list effective presentation techniques for fashion ideas.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper posture and body language during a presentation.
The students should be able to explain how to structure a fashion presentation.
The students should be able to identify visual aids that enhance fashion presentations.
Introduction:
Today we will learn how to present fashion ideas effectively. We have already created portfolios, and now we need to know how to talk about our designs in a way that captures attention and communicates our vision clearly.
Content:
Presentation skills are abilities that help you communicate your fashion ideas clearly and confidently to others. Good presentation skills are important for fashion designers when showing their work to clients, teachers, or potential employers.
Effective presentation techniques include:
1. Knowing your audience and tailoring your language accordingly
2. Practicing your speech beforehand to build confidence
3. Using clear, descriptive language to explain your design choices
4. Maintaining eye contact with your audience
5. Speaking at an appropriate volume and pace
6. Using gestures to emphasize important points
Proper posture and body language are crucial during presentations. Stand tall with your shoulders back, avoid crossing your arms, and use open gestures to appear confident and approachable. In Nigerian culture, showing respect through body language is especially important when presenting to elders or potential clients.
Structuring a fashion presentation involves organizing your ideas logically:
1. Start with an introduction of yourself and your design concept
2. Present your inspiration and mood board
3. Show your design sketches and explain your choices
4. Display photographs or samples of finished work
5. Explain any special techniques or challenges you overcame
6. Conclude with a summary and invitation for questions
Visual aids enhance presentations by making them more engaging and helping the audience understand your ideas better. Common visual aids in fashion presentations include:
- Design sketches and illustrations
- Mood boards and inspiration images
- Fabric samples and swatches
- Photographs of garments on models
- Digital presentations using PowerPoint or similar software
Class activity:
Students will prepare a 3-minute presentation about one of their favorite garment designs. They will practice proper posture, use descriptive language, and include at least one visual aid such as a sketch or fabric sample. Partners will provide constructive feedback on both content and delivery.
Evaluation questions:
1. What are three important techniques for effective fashion presentations?
2. How should a designer stand during a fashion presentation?
3. What are the main sections of a structured fashion presentation?
4. Name two visual aids that can enhance a fashion presentation.
5. Why is it important to know your audience when presenting fashion ideas?
Summary:
Effective presentation skills help fashion designers communicate their ideas clearly and confidently, using proper body language, structured content, and appropriate visual aids to engage their audience.

topics.title: Fashion Exhibition Preparation D
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify key elements of effective fashion exhibition displays.
The students should be able to explain different arrangement techniques for fashion exhibitions.
The students should be able to plan a simple fashion exhibition layout.
The students should be able to list materials needed for fashion exhibition displays.
Introduction:
Today we will learn about preparing for fashion exhibitions, which are events where designers showcase their collections. We have already learned about portfolios and presentations, and now we need to know how to display our work effectively in an exhibition setting.
Content:
A fashion exhibition is a display of fashion items in a public space to showcase a designer's work, trends, or collections. Effective exhibition displays attract attention and allow viewers to appreciate the details of each garment.
Key elements of effective fashion exhibition displays include:
1. Good lighting that highlights the garments without causing glare
2. Appropriate mannequins that complement the clothing style
3. Clear signage with designer names and garment information
4. Adequate spacing between displays to allow viewers to move comfortably
5. Cohesive theme or color scheme that ties the exhibition together
6. Background elements that enhance rather than distract from the garments
Arrangement techniques for fashion exhibitions:
1. Chronological arrangement - displaying garments in order of creation or historical period
2. Color arrangement - organizing garments by color to create visual harmony
3. Theme arrangement - grouping items by a common theme such as "traditional Nigerian attire" or "sustainable fashion"
4. Focal point arrangement - creating a central display that draws attention, with supporting pieces around it
5. Height variation - using different levels to create visual interest and guide the viewer's eye
Materials needed for fashion exhibition displays:
- Mannequins or dress forms
- Display racks and hangers
- Lighting equipment
- Signage and labels
- Backdrops and curtains
- Pins, clips, and other garment fasteners
- Padding and shaping materials for mannequins
In Nigerian fashion exhibitions, it's common to incorporate local elements like Adire fabric patterns or traditional Nigerian motifs into the display design to celebrate cultural heritage while showcasing contemporary designs.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to create a miniature fashion exhibition display on a tabletop. They will arrange garment sketches or sample pieces using at least two different arrangement techniques, create simple signage, and plan appropriate lighting using flashlights or phone lights.
Evaluation questions:
1. What are three key elements of effective fashion exhibition displays?
2. Explain how chronological arrangement differs from theme arrangement in fashion exhibitions.
3. Name two materials needed for setting up a fashion exhibition display.
4. Why is proper lighting important in fashion exhibition displays?
5. How could a Nigerian designer incorporate local cultural elements into an exhibition display?
Summary:
Effective fashion exhibition displays require careful planning of arrangement techniques, display materials, and visual elements to showcase garments in their best light and create an engaging experience for viewers.

topics.title: Fashion Show Project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the components needed to plan a fashion show.
The students should be able to explain the roles of different team members in a fashion show.
The students should be able to create a simple timeline for organizing a fashion show.
The students should be able to describe different types of fashion show formats.
Introduction:
Today we will learn about planning and coordinating a mini fashion show. We have studied portfolios, presentations, and exhibition displays, and now we will apply these skills to organize a dynamic fashion event that showcases our designs.
Content:
A fashion show is an event where models walk on a runway wearing garments designed by fashion designers. It is an exciting way to present a collection to an audience of potential buyers, media, and fashion enthusiasts.
Components needed to plan a fashion show:
1. Venue selection - appropriate space with a runway and seating area
2. Date and time consideration - avoiding major holidays and considering local events
3. Budget planning - allocating funds for venue, models, makeup, hair, photography, and marketing
4. Garment selection - choosing which designs to showcase and in what order
5. Model casting - selecting models who can properly display the garments
6. Music selection - choosing appropriate background music that complements the collection
7. Lighting design - planning lighting to highlight the garments effectively
8. Marketing and promotion - inviting guests and creating awareness about the event
Roles of different team members in a fashion show:
1. Fashion designer - creates the garments and oversees the creative direction
2. Show director - coordinates all aspects of the show and manages the team
3. Stylist - selects garments for each model and ensures proper fitting
4. Makeup artist - applies makeup that complements the garments and enhances the models' features
5. Hair stylist - creates hairstyles that work with the overall look
6. Models - walk the runway and showcase the garments professionally
7. Photographer/videographer - documents the event for promotional use
8. Stage manager - ensures smooth transitions between model appearances
9. Front of house staff - greet guests and manage seating
Types of fashion show formats:
1. Traditional runway show - models walk down a long runway with seating on both sides
2. In-the-round show - circular runway with seating all around, creating a more intimate experience
3. Static show - garments are displayed on mannequins or models in a fixed location
4. Interactive show - audience participation elements incorporated into the presentation
5. Digital/virtual show - presented online through streaming platforms
In Nigeria, fashion shows often incorporate traditional music and dance elements, and may feature garments that blend contemporary designs with traditional Nigerian fabrics like Aso Oki, Akwete, or Adire.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to plan a mini fashion show for their class. Each group will develop a concept, select 5-7 garments to showcase, create a simple timeline, assign team member roles, and design a basic floor plan for the runway and seating area.
Evaluation questions:
1. List three components needed to plan a fashion show.
2. What is the role of a show director in a fashion show?
3. How does a traditional runway show differ from an in-the-round show?
4. Name two traditional Nigerian fabrics that might be featured in a Nigerian fashion show.
5. Why is model selection important in a fashion show?
Summary:
Planning a fashion show requires coordinating many components and team members to create a successful event that showcases fashion designs effectively to an audience.

topics.title: Mid-Term Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge of portfolio development.
The students should be able to apply presentation skills in a written format.
The students should be able to identify key concepts of fashion exhibition preparation.
The students should be able to recall components of fashion show planning.
Introduction:
Today is your mid-term examination. This test will assess your understanding of the topics we have covered this term, including portfolio development, presentation skills, fashion exhibition preparation, and fashion show planning.
Content:
The examination will consist of multiple-choice questions, short answer questions, and one practical planning component. You will have 45 minutes to complete all sections.
Multiple-choice section (20 points):
- Questions about portfolio components
- Questions about presentation techniques
- Questions about exhibition display elements
- Questions about fashion show planning
Short answer section (30 points):
- Explain the difference between digital and physical portfolios
- Describe three key elements of effective exhibition displays
- List the roles of three different team members in a fashion show
- Explain how to structure a fashion presentation
Practical planning component (50 points):
Create a simple plan for a mini fashion show including:
- Concept/theme
- 5 garments to showcase with brief descriptions
- Timeline with key dates and deadlines
- Team member roles and responsibilities
- Basic sketch of the runway and seating arrangement
Class activity:
The examination itself serves as the class activity for this week. Students will work independently to complete all sections of the examination within the allotted time.
Evaluation questions:
The examination questions will serve as the evaluation for this week's learning.
Summary:
The mid-term examination assesses your understanding of fashion portfolio development, presentation skills, exhibition preparation, and fashion show planning concepts covered in the first half of the term.

topics.title: Portfolio Evaluation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify strengths and weaknesses in fashion portfolios.
The students should be able to apply evaluation criteria to assess portfolio quality.
The students should be able to suggest improvements for portfolio weaknesses.
The students should be able to create an action plan for portfolio enhancement.
Introduction:
Today we will learn how to evaluate fashion portfolios for effectiveness and quality. We have already created our own portfolios, and now we need to develop the skills to critically assess them and make improvements.
Content:
Portfolio evaluation is the process of assessing a fashion portfolio to determine its effectiveness in showcasing design skills, creativity, and professionalism. It helps designers identify areas for improvement and create stronger presentations of their work.
Criteria for evaluating fashion portfolios:
1. Quality of work - selecting only your best pieces that demonstrate your skills
2. Cohesion - whether the portfolio has a consistent style or theme throughout
3. Presentation - how professionally the work is displayed and organized
4. Technical skill - evidence of strong drawing, sewing, and construction abilities
5. Creativity - originality and innovation in design solutions
6. Context - whether the portfolio is appropriate for its intended audience or purpose
Strengths to look for in fashion portfolios:
- Strong visual impact with clear, high-quality images
- Well-organized layout with logical flow
- Diversity of skills demonstrated across different projects
- Attention to detail in both design and presentation
- Personal style that comes through in the work
- Appropriate choice of format for the intended audience
Common weaknesses in fashion portfolios:
- Including too many pieces that dilute the impact of strong work
- Inconsistent presentation or quality across pieces
- Poor lighting or photography of garments
- Lack of context or explanation for design choices
- Outdated work that doesn't reflect current skills
- Insufficient variety in design types or techniques
In the Nigerian fashion context, portfolios should demonstrate an understanding of both contemporary trends and traditional Nigerian fashion elements. A strong portfolio might include garments that showcase innovative uses of local fabrics like Aso Oki, Adire, or Ankara.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to evaluate each other's portfolios using the evaluation criteria discussed. They will identify at least three strengths and three areas for improvement in their partner's portfolio, and provide specific suggestions for enhancement.
Evaluation questions:
1. What are four criteria used to evaluate fashion portfolios?
2. Name three common weaknesses found in fashion portfolios.
3. Why is cohesion important in a fashion portfolio?
4. How should a portfolio be tailored for different audiences?
5. What traditional Nigerian elements might strengthen a fashion portfolio?
Summary:
Effective portfolio evaluation helps designers identify strengths and weaknesses in their work, allowing them to make targeted improvements that enhance the overall impact and professionalism of their presentation.

topics.title: Mid-Term Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and recharge for the second half of the term.
The students should be able to reflect on their learning so far.
Introduction:
This week is your mid-term break, a time to rest and recharge after your hard work on portfolio development, presentation skills, exhibition preparation, and fashion show planning.
Content:
During this break, you should take time to relax and enjoy some rest. It's also a good opportunity to reflect on what you've learned so far in fashion design and garment making. Consider your strengths and areas where you'd like to improve when we return to class.
You might want to visit local markets like Balogun Market in Lagos or Ariaria Market in Abia to observe current fashion trends and see how local designers display their work. You could also sketch new design ideas inspired by traditional Nigerian garments or fabrics you encounter during the break.
Remember to return to class refreshed and ready to continue your fashion design journey with renewed energy and enthusiasm.
Class activity:
The mid-term break serves as a time for rest and reflection. No formal class activity is assigned during this break period.
Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation questions are assigned during the mid-term break period.
Summary:
Enjoy your well-deserved break and return to class ready to continue exploring the exciting world of fashion design and garment making.
